title: Google Cloud Platform Landing Zone & Organization Foundation (Enterprise)
author_notes: Effort tier: T5 (enterprise Google Cloud / identity / Gemini enablement).

Google Cloud Console / gcloud / Cloud Identity / Google Admin authored at exact detail from Google public docs; version- or preview-dependent capabilities (SCC tiers, BeyondCorp features, org-policy constraints, VPC-SC behaviors, Gemini Enterprise features) cited or flagged 'verify in your organization', never invented. IaC (Terraform / Cloud Foundation Toolkit) at the pattern level. Automation is Python (gcloud / Cloud Client Libraries) — no hardcoded credentials, no committed service-account keys, no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Stand up an enterprise-grade Google Cloud foundation the right way
problem: Moving real workloads to Google Cloud Platform without a foundation creates sprawl, inconsistent security, and cost you can't attribute. This solution builds the landing zone: the resource hierarchy (Organization → folders → projects), org policies, a least-privilege IAM baseline, centralized logging/monitoring, a shared network pattern, and naming/labeling — the secure, governed platform every later workload lands on.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the landing-zone reference: resource hierarchy, org policies, IAM baseline, logging/billing/network shape, and the Assess→Design→Configure→Pilot→Validate→Expand model.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (Organization, org-admin access, billing, gcloud/IaC toolchain, hierarchy & naming design).

Implementation Guide — build the folder/project hierarchy, apply org-policy guardrails, set the IAM baseline and groups, wire centralized audit logging + billing export, and stand up the shared-network landing pattern — pilot-first, each artifact named.

5 Python tools — assessment/discovery, a configuration or provisioning helper, a validation/report generator, a policy/guardrail check, and a scope/config helper — authentic gcloud / Cloud Client Library automation (read-only or dry-run by default; no credentials or keys in code).
Validation gates (hierarchy, guardrails enforced, logging flowing) plus Best Practices for extending the landing zone as workloads onboard.
short: Build an enterprise Google Cloud landing zone — resource hierarchy, org policies, least-privilege IAM baseline, centralized logging, shared network, naming/labeling — the governed foundation every GCP workload lands on. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
